338263.title: Equivalence between SYLTDMOR1 and moment matching
338263.statement:
Consider an LTI system with piecewise constant input and zero initial state. Choose Laguerre polynomials; Legendre polynomials with odd reduced order; Chebychev polynomials of the first kind with odd reduced order; or Chebychev polynomials of the second kind with odd reduced order. Let SYLTDMOR1 denote the time-domain model-order-reduction method presented in the source, and let $\tilde{A}$ and $\tilde{E}$ be the matrices in its Sylvester equation. **Equivalence conjecture.** SYLTDMOR1 is equivalent to the moment matching method, with expansion points chosen as the eigenvalues of the matrix pencil $(-\tilde{A},\tilde{E})$ arising in the Sylvester equation; these points depend on the chosen orthogonal polynomials and the reduced order.

The claim concerns the connection between Laguerre-based time-domain model reduction and moment matching. The paper reports numerical evidence for the required distinctness of the generalized eigenvalues, while the analogous equivalence for SYLTDMOR2 is stated as a theorem. The conjecture is resolved: the equivalence between Laguerre-based time-domain model reduction and moment matching was proved by Eid.
338263.source_name: Manuela Hund and Jens Saak, “A Connection Between Time Domain Model Order Reduction and Moment Matching for LTI Systems”, arXiv:1801.07085 (2018).
338263.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.07085

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2018). “The equivalence between the Laguerre based time domain MOR and moment matching has been proven rigorously by Eid in .”

338731.title: The dense subgraph detection conjecture
338731.statement:
Let $\mathbb{G}_n$ be the set of graphs with $n$ vertices, and let $G(n,1/2)$ and $G(n,1/2,k,q)$ denote the null and alternative graph distributions, respectively. For a sequence $k=k_n$ satisfying $k\le n^\beta$ for some $0<\beta<1/2$, let $q\in(1/2,1]$, and consider tests $\psi_n:\mathbb{G}_n\to\{0,1\}$, where $\mathbf{P}_0$ and $\mathbf{P}_1$ denote probabilities under the null and alternative hypotheses.

**The dense subgraph detection conjecture.** For any sequence of randomized polynomial-time tests $(\psi_n)_n$,

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\left\{\mathbf{P}_0(\psi_n(A)=1)+\mathbf{P}_1(\psi_n(A)=0)\right\}\ge \frac{1}{3}.
$$

Equivalently, no randomized polynomial-time algorithm can correctly identify the dense subgraph with probability tending to $1$. This conjecture is used to establish a computational lower bound for matrix logistic regression; its resolution is not given in the source.
338731.source_name: Nicolai Baldin and Quentin Berthet, “Optimal link prediction with matrix logistic regression”, arXiv:1803.07054 (2018).
338731.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07054

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2018).

338974.title: Snake-decomposition characterization of c-Cambrian order element posets
338974.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be a finite root system, let $c$ be a Coxeter element, and let $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)$ denote the set of $\Phi$-posets. Let $\mathsf{COEP}(c)$ be the set of $c$-Cambrian order element posets and $\mathsf{COIP}(c)$ the set of $c$-Cambrian order interval posets. A $c$-snake is a sequence of roots satisfying the alternating sign and order conditions described in the source, and a **$c$-snake decomposition** of a root $\alpha$ is an expression $\alpha=\sum_{i\in[p]}\lambda_i\alpha_i$ with $\lambda_i\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_p$ a $c$-snake in the poset.

**Snake-decomposition characterization.** A $\Phi$-poset $\mathrel{\mathop{\rel}}\in\mathcal{P}(\Phi)$ is in $\mathsf{COEP}(c)$ if and only if it is in $\mathsf{COIP}(c)$ and every root $\alpha\in\Phi$ admits a $c$-snake decomposition in $\mathrel{\mathop{\rel}}$.

This characterizes $c$-Cambrian order element posets in terms of $c$-Cambrian order interval posets and snake decompositions. It was proved in type $A$ and checked computationally for small Coxeter types; its general status is not resolved in the supplied source.
338974.source_name: Joël Gay and Vincent Pilaud, “The weak order on Weyl posets”, arXiv:1804.06572 (2018).
338974.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06572

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

339049.title: Edelman–Greene maximality and height conjecture
339049.statement:
Let $Q\in\mathrm{SYT}(\mathrm{sc}_n)$, let $c(Q)$ be its column word, let $\mathcal{P}_Q$ be the associated poset, and let $\mathrm{EG}^{-1}(Q)$ be its inverse Edelman–Greene image. Let $h(P)$ denote the length of the longest chain in a poset $P$, and define

$$
\ell_Q=h\left([c(Q),\mathrm{EG}^{-1}(Q)]\right).
$$

**Edelman–Greene height conjecture.** The word $\mathrm{EG}^{-1}(Q)$ is a maximal element of $\mathcal{P}_Q$, and

$$
\ell_Q=\sum_{i=1}^{\operatorname{len}(c(Q))}\left(\mathrm{EG}^{-1}(Q)_i-c(Q)_i\right).
$$

The first assertion restates the preceding maximality conjecture, while the equality is motivated by computations for $Q\in\mathrm{SYT}(\mathrm{sc}_n)$. The source notes that the maximal element is not generally unique and gives no evidence that the height equality has been proved.
339049.source_name: Svante Linusson and Samu Potka, “Properties of the Edelman-Greene bijection”, arXiv:1804.10034 (2019).
339049.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.10034

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

339076.title: The two-shifted q-Motzkin determinant factorization conjecture
339076.statement:
Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_n(q)$ be defined by

$$
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_{n+1}(q)=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_n(q)+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}q^{k+1}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_k(q)\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_{n-k-1}(q),\qquad \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_0(q)=1.
$$

Define

$$
f_n(q)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{1\leq k\leq n\\k\not\equiv1\pmod 3}}q^k,&n\equiv0\pmod3,\\[4pt]\displaystyle(q+1)\left(\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}q^{3k}\right),&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

**Factorization conjecture.** We have

$$
\left(\det\left[\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_{i+j+2}(q)\right]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\right)_{n=1}^{\infty}=\bigl(q^{c_n}f_n(q)\bigr)_{n=1}^{\infty}
$$

for some $c_n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$.
The conjecture is based on numerical computations and concerns the factorization pattern of the second shifted Hankel determinants; no proof is supplied.
339076.source_name: Se-jin Oh and Travis Scrimshaw, “Identities from representation theory”, arXiv:1805.00113 (2018).
339076.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00113

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

339553.title: Seed's conjectures on reduced Szabó homology and its spectral sequence
339553.statement:
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ be a link diagram, let $p$ and $p'$ be points that are not double points of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$, and let $\widetilde{\operatorname{CSz}}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}},p)$ denote Szabó homology reduced at $p$. Let $E^k$ be the Leray spectral sequence from the homological filtration on $\operatorname{CSz}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}})$, and let $\widetilde{E}^k$ be the corresponding spectral sequence on $\widetilde{\operatorname{CSz}}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}},p)$. The notation $\{\pm1\}$ denotes a shift in quantum grading. **Seed's conjectures.**

1. $\widetilde{\operatorname{CSz}}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}},p) \cong \widetilde{\operatorname{CSz}}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}},p')$.
2. (Twin arrows) 

$$
E^k(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}) \cong \widetilde{E}^k(L)\{-1\} \oplus \widetilde{E}^k(L)\{1\}.
$$

3. If $K$ is a knot, then $E^k(K)$ is invariant under mutation for $k \geq 2$.
4. Szabó homology is isomorphic to mirror Szabó homology.

These conjectures are presented as further conjectures motivated by Seed's computations and the preceding Szabó–Heegaard Floer conjecture; the source does not report a resolution.
339553.source_name: Adam Saltz, “Mutation-invariance of Khovanov-Floer theories”, arXiv:1806.05595 (2018).
339553.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.05595

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

339832.title: Positivity for the $C_\alpha$ refinement
339832.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be the ring of symmetric functions, let $\nabla$ and the Delta operators act on it, and let $\phi$ be defined by

$$
\phi f[X]=f[MX].
$$

For a composition $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{\ell(\alpha)})$, define

$$
C_\alpha=\mathbb{C}_{\alpha_1}\mathbb{C}_{\alpha_2}\cdots\mathbb{C}_{\alpha_{\ell(\alpha)}}(1),
$$

where the operators $\mathbb{C}_m$ are those of Haglund, Morse, and Zabrocki. **Positivity conjecture.** For any composition $\alpha\vDash n-\ell$,

$$
\left\langle \Delta_{\phi\Delta_{e_{\ell}}\phi^{-1}(h_pe_{n-d})}\nabla C_\alpha,h_{n-\ell}\right\rangle\in\mathbb{N}[q,t].
$$

This conjecture predicts coefficientwise positivity in $q$ and $t$ for a compositional refinement of the generalized Delta setting. It is presented as computer-supported evidence, and no resolution is supplied in the source.
339832.source_name: Michele D'Adderio, Alessandro Iraci and Anna Vanden Wyngaerd, “The Schröder case of the generalized Delta conjecture”, arXiv:1807.05413 (2018).
339832.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05413

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).

340156.title: Regularity bound by the h-polynomial degree for binomial edge ideals
340156.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on the vertex set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $K[\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}]=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring over a field $K$, and let $J_G$ be the binomial edge ideal generated by $x_i y_j-x_j y_i$ for the edges $\{i,j\}$ of $G$. Write

$$
h_{K[\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}]/J_G}(\lambda)=h_0+h_1\lambda+\cdots+h_s\lambda^s
$$

for the $h$-polynomial of $K[\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}]/J_G$, and let $\operatorname{reg}$ denote Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity. **Regularity–$h$-degree conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{reg}(K[\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}]/J_G)\leq \deg h_{K[\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}]/J_G}(\lambda).
$$

Equality is known when the quotient is Cohen--Macaulay, but the inequality is supported here only by computational experience and remains open in general.
340156.source_name: Takayuki Hibi and Kazunori Matsuda, “Regularity and h-polynomials of binomial edge ideals”, arXiv:1808.06984 (2020).
340156.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.06984

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

341256.title: Hexagon conditional local-move conjecture for punctured-disk resistor networks
341256.statement:
Consider a local transformation of a resistor-network subgraph with a central interior boundary vertex, six incident edges with conductances $a,b,c,d,e,f$, a surrounding hexagonal configuration with conductances $g,h,i,j,k,\ell$, and four additional external edges with conductances $m,n,o,p$, together with the corresponding transformed graph with conductances $A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I,J,K,L,M,N,O,P,Q$. The transformation is the hexagon conditional local move depicted in the source.

**Hexagon conditional local-move conjecture.** There is a hexagon conditional local move of the displayed form, with the conjectural conductance formulas described in the paper, that preserves the response matrix.

The formulas were checked to preserve every response-matrix entry except the entry in the row and column corresponding to the interior boundary vertex; that computation was too large to complete, although several numerical choices gave equal response matrices. Thus the conjecture remains open.
341256.source_name: Yulia Alexandr, Brian Burks, Sunita Chepuri and Patricia Commins, “Recovering Conductances of Resistor Networks in a Punctured Disk”, arXiv:1812.01517 (2018).
341256.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.01517

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

341292.title: The final-matrix exponential-pattern conjecture
341292.statement:
Let $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)$ denote the final-matrix value and let $\mathrm{ST}_n$ be the recursively defined Sierpinski-triangle set. **Exponential-pattern conjecture $(SE_n)$.** Suppose that $i,j\in\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}$. Then:

1. $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)>0$ if and only if $i$ is even, $j$ is odd, and $(i+1,j)\in\mathrm{ST}_n$.
2. If $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)>0$, then $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)=2^i$.
3. If $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)<0$, then $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)=-2^k$ for some $k$. Furthermore:
 - if $j$ is odd, then $0<k\leq i$, $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^{i'},2^j)=-2^k$ for $k\leq i'\leq i$, and $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^{k-1},2^j)=2^{k-1}$;
 - if $j$ is even and $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^{j+1})>0$, then $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)=-FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^{j+1})$;
 - if $j$ is even and $FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^{j+1})<0$, then $2\cdot FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^j)=FM_{2^n}^{-}(2^i,2^{j+1})$.

The conjecture was experimentally verified for $n\leq5$, but the excerpt also states that, assuming a rank-into-rank cardinal, some $n$ makes $(SE_n)$ false. Thus its universal form is refuted relative to that stated hypothesis.
341292.source_name: Joseph Van Name, “Generalizations of Laver tables”, arXiv:1812.02761 (2018).
341292.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02761

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2018); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

343536.title: Equitable partitions of rectangular grid graphs
343536.statement:
Let $P_m\oblong P_n$ be the rectangular grid graph, and let its automorphism group act naturally on its vertices. An equitable partition is a partition in which every vertex in a cell has the same number of neighbors in each cell.

**Grid-graph equitable-partition conjecture.** The equitable partitions of $P_m\oblong P_n$ are the orbit partitions of natural actions of the subgroups of the automorphism group of the graph. The lattice of equitable partitions is isomorphic to the lattice of subgroups exactly when there is a vertex with trivial stabilizer subgroup. This happens unless $2\le m=n\le3$.

The claim concerns the relationship between equitable partitions and symmetry-induced orbit partitions for rectangular grid graphs. The supplied text reports this as an apparent pattern based on computations, but gives no resolution or proof.
343536.source_name: John M. Neuberger, Nandor Sieben and James W. Swift, “Invariant synchrony subspaces of sets of matrices”, arXiv:1908.05797 (2020).
343536.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1807.10954](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.10954).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.05797

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

343979.title: Hinman's generalized period conjecture for Ulam sequences U(1,n)
343979.statement:
For integers $1\leq a<b$, let $U(a,b)$ be the Ulam sequence whose later terms are the smallest integers representable as sums of two distinct prior terms in exactly one way. For a positive real number $\lambda$, reduction modulo $\lambda$ is taken using representatives in an interval of length $\lambda$. **Hinman's generalized period conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq2$, there exist real numbers $\lambda_n$ and $K_n$ such that, for every $\epsilon>0$,

$$
U(1,n)\cap[K_n,\infty)\mod\lambda_n\subset\left(\frac{\lambda_n}{3}-\epsilon,\frac{2\lambda_n}{3}+\epsilon\right).
$$

Furthermore, for $n\geq4$, one can take $\lambda_n=3n+\lambda'$, where $\lambda'\approx0.417031$. This folklore generalization is supported by numerical evidence; the asymptotic statement is not proved in the source.
343979.source_name: Arseniy Sheydvasser, “The Ulam Sequence of the Integer Polynomial Ring”, arXiv:1910.00109 (2021).
343979.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.00109

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

344161.title: The specialization conjecture for symmetry-breaking link homology
344161.statement:
Let $L$ be a link, let $E^{\ast,\ast}_2(L,\overline{\theta})$ denote the $E_2$-page associated to the specialized twist $\overline{\theta}$, and let $\wp(x)=x^n$ be the algebraic specialization. The groups $E^{\ast,\ast}_q(L,\overline{\theta})$ denote the pages of the resulting spectral sequence.

**Specialization conjecture.** Under the algebraic specialization $\wp(x)=x^n$, the groups

$$
E^{\ast,\ast}_2(L,\overline{\theta})
$$

are isomorphic to $sl(n)$-link homology. This specialization has a topological lift, meaning that it can be lifted to a map of filtered spectra. Consequently, there is a spectral sequence

$$
E^{\ast,\ast}_q(L,\overline{\theta}),\qquad q\geq 2.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computations for the Hopf link and the $(2,3)$-torus knot. The proposed topological lift is intended to provide a route toward resolving the conjecture.
344161.source_name: Nitu Kitchloo, “Symmetry Breaking and Link Homologies II”, arXiv:1910.07444 (2023).
344161.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07444

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

344785.title: The cube-root fluctuation conjecture for the LCS concatenation gain
344785.statement:
Let $V$ and $W$ be independent random words of length $2n$, written as concatenations $V=V_1V_2$ and $W=W_1W_2$, where each component has length $n$. Define

$$
\Delta(V,W)=\operatorname{LCS}(V,W)-\operatorname{LCS}(V_1,W_1)-\operatorname{LCS}(V_2,W_2),
$$

and write $\Delta(2n)=\Delta(V,W)$. **Cube-root fluctuation conjecture.** There are constants $c_1,c_2$ such that

$$
\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}\Delta(n)\sim c_1n^{1/3}
$$

and

$$
\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}\Delta(n)}\sim c_2n^{1/3}.
$$

The conjecture is suggested by the paper’s computational experiments on the excess LCS obtained by allowing matches to cross the two concatenated blocks. The cited prior estimate gives only the upper-order control $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}\Delta(V,W)=O(\sqrt{n\log n})$, so the cube-root asymptotics remain open.
344785.source_name: Boris Bukh and Christopher Cox, “Periodic words, common subsequences and frogs”, arXiv:1912.03510 (2021).
344785.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.03510

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

344963.title: Tightness of the compact formulation for min-stop ramping constraints
344963.statement:
Let the single-unit subproblem be defined by constraints $$--$$, and let UCPd denote the discrete Unit Commitment problem with min-stop ramping constraints. The associated polytope is the convex hull of the feasible integer points for the min-stop ramping constraints.

**Tightness conjecture.** The polytope defined for a single unit with constraints $$--$$ describes the convex hull of the feasible integer points for the min-stop ramping constraints. Equivalently, the ILP formulation given by these constraints is tight, and the Dantzig--Wolfe reformulation of UCPd obtained by dualizing demand and reserve constraints has the same LP relaxation as the compact formulation of section 4 and the other tightest equivalent formulation derived by Dupin et al.

The conjecture is motivated by empirical equality of the LP-relaxation values in the considered instances. The source reports that it was verified by computing the subproblems as LPs or ILPs during column-generation iterations.
344963.source_name: Nicolas Dupin, “Column generation for the discrete Unit Commitment problem with min-stop ramping constraints”, arXiv:1912.09255 (2019).
344963.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09255

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2019). “This conjecture was verified computing sub-problems ()-() as LP or ILP during CG iterations.”

352683.title: The exact piercing-number conjecture for the chessboard
352683.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n\times n$ chessboard, and let $p_n$ denote the minimum number of lines whose union intersects every cell of $Q_n$. **Piercing-number conjecture.** For all $n \geq 3$, 
$$
p_n=n-1.
$$
 The conjecture would determine the exact piercing number of the chessboard. The preceding results establish the upper bound $p_n\leq n-1$ for $n\geq 3$ and the asymptotic lower bound $p_n>0.7n$ for sufficiently large $n$; the claimed equality remains open, motivated in the source by a computer search finding no configuration of $n-2$ lines for $n\leq 15$.
352683.source_name: Gergely Ambrus, Imre Bárány, Péter Frankl and Dániel Varga, “Piercing the chessboard”, arXiv:2111.09702 (2023).
352683.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.09702

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

364816.title: Random planar bipartite-coloring approximation conjecture
364816.statement:
Let $P_n$ consist of $n$ independent random points uniformly distributed in $[0,1]^2$, and let a bipartite coloring of $P_n$ be any coloring induced by a Euclidean minimum spanning tree. **Random bipartite-coloring approximation conjecture.** The maximum EMST-ratio is less than $1.1$ times any bipartite EMST-ratio of the point set with probability tending to $1$ as $n$ goes to infinity.

Computational experiments reported in the source found that the maximum EMST-ratio was at most $1.3$ times, and rarely more than $1.1$ times, the computed bipartite EMST-ratio for the tested random point sets. The asymptotic claim remains open.
364816.source_name: Afrouz Jabal Ameli, Faezeh Motiei and Morteza Saghafian, “On the MST-ratio: Theoretical Bounds and Complexity of Finding the Maximum”, arXiv:2409.11079 (2025).
364816.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11079

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

366032.title: The superexponential coefficient-growth conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
366032.statement:
For $w\in\mathrm{S}_{n}$, let $\mathrm{P}_{w}$ be the first-row Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial, and let $\mathrm{coeff}_{n}$ denote the maximal coefficient among these polynomials; let $\mathrm{ev}_{n}$ denote the corresponding maximal value at $\mathtt{v}=1$. **Superexponential coefficient-growth conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{coeff}_{n}\in\Omega(\gamma^{n})\quad\text{for all }\gamma\in\mathbb{R}_{>1}.
$$

Since $\mathrm{ev}_{n}\geq\mathrm{coeff}_{n}$, the same superexponential lower bound is asserted for $\mathrm{ev}_{n}$. The evidence is computational, and the conjecture concerns the asymptotic growth of the largest coefficients and evaluations.
366032.source_name: Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer and Pedro Vaz, “Big data approach to Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials”, arXiv:2412.01283 (2026).
366032.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01283

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

369840.title: Hankel total positivity conjecture for vincular pattern Classes 1 and 2
369840.statement:
For each $n\geq 0$, let $P_n^{(1)}(x)$ and $P_n^{(2)}(x)$ be the generating polynomials for the number of occurrences of vincular patterns in Class $1$ and Class $2$, respectively. A polynomial sequence is **coefficientwise Hankel totally positive** in $x$ when every minor of its Hankel matrix has coefficients that are nonnegative polynomials in $x$.

**Hankel total positivity conjecture.** The sequences of polynomials

$$
\left(P_n^{(1)}(x+1)\right)_{n\geq 0},\qquad \left(P_n^{(2)}(x+1)\right)_{n\geq 0}
$$

are both coefficientwise Hankel totally positive with respect to the variable $x$.

The unshifted sequences are not coefficientwise Hankel totally positive, while computations suggest that the shift $x\mapsto x+1$ restores this stronger positivity property. The claim is supported by finite tests but remains open.
369840.source_name: Bishal Deb, “Cyclic sieving phenomena via combinatorics of continued fractions”, arXiv:2508.13709 (2025).
369840.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2507.18959](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18959), [arXiv:2105.05583](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05583), [arXiv:1807.01062](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.01062), [arXiv:1807.03271](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03271).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13709

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

373759.title: The MDS probability convergence conjecture
373759.statement:
Let $C$ be a linear $[n,k]$ code chosen uniformly at random over a field $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $n,q\to\infty$. The property **MDS** means that the minimum distance of $C$ is $n-k+1$.

**MDS probability convergence conjecture.** If

$$
\frac{1}{q}\binom{n}{k}\to\lambda\in(0,\infty),
$$

then

$$
P(C\text{ is MDS})\to e^{-\lambda}.
$$

The source notes that this extends the known asymptotic result beyond the regime $k/n\to0$, and leaves the assertion open while providing numerical evidence for the case $n=2k$.
373759.source_name: Rathinakumar Appuswamy, Marco Bazzani, Spencer Congero, Joseph Connelly, Matthew Ekaireb and Kenneth Zeger, “Probability of super-regular matrices and MDS codes over finite fields”, arXiv:2603.20983 (2026).
373759.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20983

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “We thus leave this conjecture as an open question, but we do demonstrate some numerical results (when $n=2k$) which support the conjecture and demonstrate convergence rates.”
